stem: Using the base-case worksheet, what is the first-year ROI?

rationales.A: 28.6% divides net benefit by benefit rather than total cost.
rationales.B: Annual benefit is $75,600 and total cost is $54,000; $21,600 / $54,000 = 40%.
rationales.C: 140% is benefit divided by cost, without subtracting cost from the numerator.
rationales.D: 75% is not supported by the stated benefits and full first-year costs.

stem: Agents release 300 hours per month, but management has no plan to redeploy time or avoid costs. What should the business case report?

options.B: A measured capacity improvement, with financial realization still unproven
options.C: Both $9,000 labor savings and additional revenue from those same hours without further evidence
options.D: No operational benefit of any kind

rationales.A: Hours valued at a labor rate do not establish an actual cash saving.
rationales.B: This distinguishes observed time improvement from the additional evidence needed for financial value.
rationales.C: This risks double counting; distinct incremental benefits require evidence.
rationales.D: Released capacity can be an operational benefit even before financial realization is established.

stem: Assisted-ticket coverage falls to 25%, with other worksheet assumptions unchanged. Which conclusion is supported?

options.A: Year-one ROI remains 40% because software cost is unchanged
options.B: Year-one ROI becomes −30%; investigate adoption and realized value before scaling
options.C: The model proves that all support assistants are uneconomic
options.D: Immediately double the labor rate used in the business case

rationales.A: Benefits decline with assistance coverage even though this model holds cost fixed.
rationales.B: Annual benefit becomes $37,800, net benefit −$16,200 and ROI −30%. This is a conditional scenario.
rationales.C: One set of assumptions about one workflow does not support a general claim.
rationales.D: Changing a rate to improve the conclusion is unjustified without new evidence.

stem: A positive-ROI pilot reduces first-response time but substantially increases repeat contacts. What is the strongest next action?

options.A: Scale because the reported ROI is positive
options.B: Remove repeat contacts from the quality dashboard
options.C: Investigate total resolution effort and quality before a scale decision
options.D: Replace all customer satisfaction measures with model usage counts

rationales.A: The ROI may omit downstream rework and the quality constraint has not been met.
rationales.B: Removing adverse evidence undermines the decision.
rationales.C: Repeated contacts can offset time savings and harm customers; evaluate full workflow outcomes before proceeding.
rationales.D: Usage is an adoption signal, not sufficient evidence of customer value or quality.

stem: Choose TWO recurring costs to include when evaluating this assistant beyond the upfront implementation fee.

options.C: The entire baseline support payroll plus the same saved hours again as a new cost
options.D: Only costs that make the preferred option appear cheaper

rationales.A: Model or software usage is part of operating the solution.
rationales.B: Monitoring and evaluation consume resources needed to sustain acceptable outcomes.
rationales.C: Use a consistent incremental model; avoid adding an unchanged baseline as a new project cost or double counting saved time.
rationales.D: Cost selection must be complete and evidence-based, independent of the preferred conclusion.

stem: At base coverage, realization falls from 70% to 40%. What does the worksheet imply?

options.A: ROI is −20%, so realization is a decision-critical assumption
options.B: ROI is unchanged because agents still release 300 hours
options.D: Payback is guaranteed within 5.45 calendar months of signing

rationales.A: Recognized annual benefit is $43,200 against $54,000 cost, giving −20% ROI.
rationales.B: Released hours remain constant, but recognized value declines.
rationales.C: Financial realization alone does not establish output accuracy.
rationales.D: The original payback assumed different realization and excluded implementation delay and ramp.
